description.narrative:
The resurgence of the M23 rebel group in North and South Kivu has escalated conflict, leading
to increased sexual violence and displacement. The reduction in USAID funding has further
restricted the ability of humanitarian organizations to provide essential medical care. This note
seeks additional donor support to procure PEP kits and contraceptives, ensuring continued
treatment for sexual violence survivors.
General description and link with proposal:
Cordaid already implements a project S3G, that is working with local health centers to increased quantity and
quality of SRH and SGBV care.
The S3G II project aims to contribute to greater stability in North and South Kivu by addressing the VSGB and SRHR
needs of the population, focusing on greater and uninterrupted access to SRHR products and services, gender
equity, partnership and local ownership.

Three strategic areas have been identified to achieve this objective, namely :
§ Strengthening the multi-sectoral response to gender-based violence through the operation of one-stop
centers (health, psychosocial support, juridical help and socio economical support), with a focus on
empowering survivors and building their resilience. More specifically: Medical care consists of the
reception of survivors, respecting confidentiality and consent, stabilization, physical examination with an
emphasis on the collection of medico-legal evidence, care of lesions, administration of the PEP Kit,
contraceptives, antibiotics and then psychosocial care

Total beneficiaries: 13 774 People. Women: Children: Men: Elderly: Disabled: Explain how direct beneficiaries are selected or targeted: Within 44 health facilities, beneficiaries will be identified and targeted according to the needs expressed by health providers.
